title: Copperlark Insurance LLM concierge jot
summary: Working scratchpad capturing the intake call and technical triage for Copperlark Insurance's concierge assistant pilot. Focus: private deployment (VPC), PII handling, latency SLOs, and rollout path from PoC to dedicated capacity.
content:
Call: Copperlark onboarding (2026-02-26) - intake + tech triage
Attendees: Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Redwood Security), Samir (Copperlark lead eng), Lina Ortiz (Copperlark product), Rajesh Menon (Copperlark infra)

High level ask
- Concierge assistant for claims triage and benefits guidance.
- Must run in Copperlark VPC (customer-managed) with private control plane.
- Initial scope: answer policy questions, summarize uploaded claim notes, redact PII and surface next steps.
- Volume: ~50 qps peak during business hours; 500k requests/month expected.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation end-to-end <= 300ms for short replies (<= 150 tokens).

Security & data residency
- Copperlark requires customer-managed KMS (HSM optional) and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.
- Must support FIPS endpoints for key operations.
- No model telemetry allowed outside VPC for PII payloads; logs should be stored in their S3 with lifecycle 365d.
- Action: check our Private deployment image with KMS plugin (PR linked: ops#482). Priya to validate FIPS compatibility (JIRA-RED-2147).

Model & inference choices (triage notes)
- Recommend medium open model (Redwood-verified) quantized to int8 with KV cache enabled — tradeoffs: cost vs hallucination risk on domain questions.
- For initial PoC use redwood/forte-7b-int8 (simulated name) with prompt templates constrained to structured outputs.
- Fallback policy: if dedicated nodes busy, route to smaller variant or return short summary + escalate to human. Plan routing policy in config: region -> private -> dedicated pool -> hosted-fallback (if allowed).

Latency and batching considerations
- Target batch size 1 for interactive concierge; allow micro-batching up to 4 for bursts. Use adaptive batching window (5-8ms) to avoid p95 spikes.
- Enable prefix caching for repeated policy lookups; set prefix TTL = 10m and cold-start penalty measurement.
- Measure p50/p95 across input length buckets (<=50 tokens, 51-150, 151-400).

PII detection and redaction
- Two-stage approach: pre-send client-side deterministic redactor for SSNs/CCNs, then server-side LLM check with a strict extractor to redact before logs persist.
- Keep redaction deterministic (hashing + token replacement) and store mapping only in Copperlark vault if requested.
- Action: create prompt-level guardrails and a JSON schema output for any summary (fields: summary_text, redacted_entities[]).

Operational controls and observability
- Need per-route cost/latency breakdown in Console; tag routes by product: claims-triage-prod, claims-triage-dev.
- Integrations requested: Datadog traces, CloudWatch export, and Copperlark SIEM via syslog.
- Alerting: token-cost spike, p95 > 350ms, error rate >1%.

Edge cases & gotchas mentioned in call
- Customer wants deterministic short answers for policy lookup (avoid creative paraphrase). May require fine-tuning or ensembles of retrieval + LLM.
- PDFs with scanned attachments: OCR quality varies; propose preprocessing pipeline (Textract) and confidence threshold before invoking model.
- Insurance legal wants transcripts retained for 7 years, but security ops wants minimal retention — need legal signoff.

Migration path / rollout plan
1) PoC (2-4 weeks): private deployment in their dev VPC, one model variant, basic redaction, sample routes. Measure latency and cost.
2) Pilot (8-12 weeks): scale to dedicated capacity in region, integrate SIEM logs, implement fallback policies.
3) Prod (Q3): SLA + reserved capacity contract, long-term retention agreement.

Action items (owners + rough due dates)
- Priya: verify KMS/FIPS compatibility and HSM options (JIRA-RED-2147) — due 2026-03-05.
- Diego: stand up private control plane image and share install notes with Rajesh; attach ops#482 — due 2026-03-10.
- Maya: produce PoC runbook (step-by-step) + minimal prompt templates and schema examples — due 2026-03-03.
- Rajesh (Copperlark): provide VPC peering details, SIEM endpoint, and sample datasets (anonymized) — due 2026-03-04.
- Samir: confirm expected max sequence length and provide corpus stats (avg tokens, attachments percent) — due 2026-03-04.

Open questions to resolve
- Legal retention window finalization (7y vs 1y) — who signs off? (Legal + Security)
- Is hosted-fallback allowed for redacted-only traffic? Need policy decision.
- OCR pipeline SLA and where preprocessing runs (customer side vs Redwood).

Notes to self / friction points
- Private deploy installs often fail on MTU/peering defaults; include troubleshooting checklist.
- Watch for kernel incompat on older NVIDIA drivers; ensure our runtime auto-falls back to compatible kernels.
- Quantization testing required: run evals on our prompt set to check answer fidelity before enabling int8 in prod.

Quick test plan ideas
- Create 200 synthetic claim notes with edge PII patterns and run redaction + summary pipeline; measure false redaction and miss rates.
- Latency sweep: 10k requests across buckets at target burst levels to validate p95 < 300ms.
- Quality A/B: int8 vs fp16 on same prompts, compare factuality and hallucination rates on an eval set.

Next sync: Thursday 2026-03-04, 10:00 PT — include Legal and Copperlark infra.

Random brainstorm (architecture):
- Consider local retrieval + small contextualizer service in customer's VPC that precomputes dense vectors and does strict candidate filtering before model call (reduce hallucinations and tokens).
- If legal insists on zero external logs, offer fully air-gapped on-prem package but note higher TCO and longer lead time.

End of jot.

References inside Redwood:
- ops#482 (private control plane image)
- JIRA-RED-2147 (KMS/FIPS evaluation)
- prompt-templates/claims-basic.json (internal repo)
